cities.name: Madurai
cities.overview: One of the oldest cities in South India and a centre of Tamil culture for over two thousand years, Madurai is built around the Meenakshi Temple and comes alive late into the night.
cities.history: An ancient city and the capital of the Pandya kings, known for its early Tamil literary academies. The Nayaks rebuilt it in the 16th and 17th centuries around the Meenakshi Temple.

cities.name: Thanjavur
cities.overview: The capital of the Chola empire at its height, Thanjavur is known for the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Tanjore paintings, bronze casting and Carnatic music.
cities.history: The capital of the Chola empire at its height, when Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswarar Temple. Later it was ruled by the Nayaks and then by a Maratha dynasty.

cities.name: Mamallapuram
cities.overview: Also called Mahabalipuram, this seaside town 55 km south of Chennai was a Pallava port. Its rock-cut temples and reliefs form a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and stone carvers still work in its streets.

cities.name: Udhagamandalam
cities.overview: Ooty, the 'Queen of Hill Stations', sits at about 2,200 metres in the Nilgiri Hills, with tea gardens, a botanical garden, a lake and cool weather all year.

cities.name: Kanyakumari
cities.overview: The southern tip of mainland India, where the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean meet. Sunrise and sunset can both be seen over the sea.

cities.name: Rameswaram
cities.overview: An island town connected to the mainland by the Pamban bridges, and one of the holiest Hindu pilgrimage sites, linked to the Ramayana.

cities.name: Karaikudi
cities.overview: The main town of the Chettinad region, known for its grand merchant mansions, antique markets, handloom saris and fiery cuisine.

cities.name: Chennai
cities.overview: Tamil Nadu's capital on the Bay of Bengal, a city of Carnatic music, old temples and colonial landmarks along a long beach.
cities.history: It grew around Fort St. George, built by the East India Company in 1639, on a coast where old villages like Mylapore already stood. As Madras, it became the seat of a large British presidency.

cities.name: Tiruchirappalli
cities.overview: A river city on the Kaveri, known for its Rockfort and the temple island of Srirangam.

cities.name: Kanchipuram
cities.overview: The city of a thousand temples, once the capital of the Pallavas, and famous for its silk sarees.

cities.name: Kumbakonam
cities.overview: A temple town between the Kaveri and Arasalar rivers, in the rice bowl of the Chola country.

cities.name: Kodaikanal
cities.overview: A hill station at 2,225 m in the Palani Hills, built around a star-shaped lake by American missionaries in 1845.

cities.name: Coimbatore
cities.overview: An industrial city by the Noyyal River, with the Anamalai hills and Ooty both within reach.

cities.name: Tiruvannamalai
cities.overview: A temple town at the foot of the sacred Arunachala hill, a favourite with spiritual seekers.

cities.name: Chidambaram
cities.overview: A temple town near the Coromandel coast, with mangroves at Pichavaram close by.

cities.name: Vellore
cities.overview: A city with a huge moated fort and the golden temple at Sripuram.

cities.name: Salem
cities.overview: A hill-ringed city in the north of the state, the base for Yercaud and the Hogenakkal falls.

cities.name: Tenkasi
cities.overview: A town in the far south at the foot of the Western Ghats, known for the Courtallam falls.

cities.name: Nagapattinam
cities.overview: A port on the Bay of Bengal, the base for the shrine at Velankanni and the Point Calimere marshes.

cities.name: Palani
cities.overview: A pilgrim town at the foot of the Palani Hills, known for its hilltop Murugan temple.

places.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
places.shortDescription: A vast temple complex with fourteen colourful gopurams covered in thousands of painted figures.
places.description: The temple is dedicated to Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort Sundareswarar (Shiva). Its gopurams are covered with brightly painted gods, demons and animals; the southern tower is about 52 metres high. Inside, explore the Hall of a Thousand Pillars, the Golden Lotus Tank, and the evening ceremony when Shiva is carried to Meenakshi's chamber for the night. Phones and cameras are not allowed inside.
places.history: The temple has ancient roots but was largely rebuilt by the Nayak rulers in the 16th and 17th centuries. Its annual Chithirai Festival celebrates the divine wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; April–May for the Chithirai Festival.

entryFee.note: Free entry; paid special darshan available.

timings.hours: About 5:00 AM – 12:30 PM and 4:00 PM – 9:30 PM

places.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
places.shortDescription: Rajaraja Chola's 1,000-year-old granite temple, whose 66-metre tower was one of the tallest in the world when built.
places.description: Also called the Big Temple or Peruvudaiyar Kovil, this Shiva temple is a masterpiece of Chola architecture. Its towering vimana is crowned by a huge granite capstone, and a monolithic Nandi bull faces the shrine. The corridors hold Chola frescoes and a long line of lingas. The granite glows in the late-afternoon sun, and the temple is still in daily worship.
places.history: Built by Rajaraja Chola I and completed in 1010 CE. It is part of the Great Living Chola Temples UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1987.

timings.hours: About 6:00 AM – 12:30 PM and 4:00 PM – 8:30 PM

location.address: Membalam Road, Balaganapathy Nagar, Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu 613007

places.name: Shore Temple, Mamallapuram
places.shortDescription: A granite Pallava temple on the edge of the Bay of Bengal, one of South India's oldest structural stone temples.
places.description: The Shore Temple's twin towers rise right beside the sea. One ticket also covers the Pancha Rathas, five chariot-shaped shrines each carved from a single rock. Free nearby are Arjuna's Penance, one of the world's largest open-air rock reliefs, and Krishna's Butter Ball, a giant boulder balanced on a slope.
places.history: Built in the early 8th century under the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha). The 2004 tsunami briefly exposed remains of other structures in the sea nearby. The monuments of Mamallapuram became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.
places.bestTimeNote: November to February. The Mamallapuram Dance Festival is held in December–January.

entryFee.note: Same ticket covers the Pancha Rathas. Children under 15 free.

location.address: Shore Temple Road, Mamallapuram, Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu 603104

sources.title: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram – UNESCO

places.name: Nilgiri Mountain Railway
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed toy train that climbs through tea estates and tunnels from Mettupalayam to Ooty.
places.description: The 46 km ride takes about five hours uphill, crossing over 200 curves, more than 200 bridges and about 16 tunnels. Between Mettupalayam and Coonoor it uses a rack-and-pinion system, India's only one, to climb the steep gradient, and the section is still worked by steam locomotives. Book seats on the right-hand side going up for the best valley views; tickets sell out quickly.
places.history: Completed in 1908, the line became part of the Mountain Railways of India UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.
places.bestTimeNote: March to June and September to November. Landslides can suspend services in heavy rain.

entryFee.note: Rail ticket; book through Indian Railways (IRCTC) well in advance.

location.address: Udhagamandalam Railway Station, Ooty, Nilgiris district, Tamil Nadu 643001

places.name: Vivekananda Rock Memorial
places.shortDescription: A memorial on a sea rock off Kanyakumari where Swami Vivekananda meditated in 1892.
places.description: Ferries take visitors from the shore to the rock, where a mandapam combines architectural styles from across India and a meditation hall looks out to sea. A glass-floored footbridge now links it to the 133-foot statue of the Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar on the neighbouring rock. Stay on the mainland for sunrise and sunset over the meeting of three seas.
places.history: Swami Vivekananda swam to the rock and meditated here for three days in December 1892, before his famous address in Chicago. The memorial was built by the Vivekananda Rock Memorial Committee and opened in 1970.

entryFee.note: Ferry and memorial entry are ticketed. Services stop in rough seas.

places.name: Ramanathaswamy Temple
places.shortDescription: A Jyotirlinga temple on Rameswaram island, famous for having the longest temple corridors in India.
places.description: Pilgrims traditionally bathe in the sea at Agni Theertham and then in the temple's 22 sacred wells before worshipping the linga said to have been installed by Lord Rama. The outer corridor is lined with more than a thousand carved pillars and runs for over a kilometre around the temple. Dress modestly; bags and phones may need to be left outside.
places.history: According to the Ramayana, Rama worshipped Shiva here after returning from Lanka. The temple was expanded over centuries, mainly by the Setupati rulers of Ramnad in the 17th and 18th centuries.

entryFee.note: Free darshan; paid special darshan and theertham bath tickets.

timings.hours: About 5:00 AM – 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM – 9:00 PM

places.name: Chettinad Mansions
places.shortDescription: Palatial merchant homes with Burma teak pillars, Italian marble and Japanese tiles across quiet Chettinad villages.
places.description: Wealthy Nattukottai Chettiar merchants built around 10,000 grand mansions across about 75 villages. Some are now heritage hotels and museums; others stand empty. In Kanadukathan and Karaikudi, see long courtyards, Athangudi tiles still made by hand, and the antique market. Stay for at least one Chettinad meal.
places.history: The mansions were built mainly between the mid-19th and mid-20th centuries with fortunes made in banking and trade across Burma, Ceylon and South-East Asia. The region is on UNESCO's Tentative List as part of 'Chettinad, Village Clusters of the Tamil Merchants'.

entryFee.note: Some mansions charge a small fee or ask for a donation; heritage hotels offer tours.

timings.hours: Usually 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM for mansions open to visitors

places.name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
places.shortDescription: A colourful Shiva temple in Mylapore with a soaring gopuram, the heart of old Chennai.
places.description: Its tower is packed with painted figures, and the temple tank is the focus of life in the old neighbourhood. The Arubathimoovar festival in spring brings out great crowds.
places.history: The present temple dates from around the 17th century.

places.name: Marina Beach
places.shortDescription: A 6 km urban beach along the Bay of Bengal, the city's evening meeting place.
places.description: One of the longest urban beaches in the world, with food stalls, kites and evening crowds. The strong current makes it unsafe for swimming.

places.name: Fort St. George
places.shortDescription: The first English fortress in India, founded in 1639, and the place where modern Chennai began.
places.description: Still in use as the state government's seat, with a fine museum of Company-era arms and coins and India's oldest Anglican church, St. Mary's.
places.history: Founded in 1639 by the East India Company, and it provided the impetus for the growth of the city.

places.name: San Thome Basilica
places.shortDescription: A white Neo-Gothic basilica built over the tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle.
places.description: One of very few churches in the world built over the tomb of an apostle. The tall white spire can be seen from the beach, and the museum tells the story of Thomas in India.
places.history: The present building dates from the late 19th century.

sources.title: St. Thomas Cathedral Basilica, Chennai – Wikipedia

places.name: Government Museum, Chennai
places.shortDescription: India's second-oldest museum, with the world's finest collection of Chola bronzes.
places.description: A red Indo-Saracenic complex at Egmore, with the Bronze Gallery as the great draw. Don't miss the Nataraja figures.
places.history: Started in 1851.

places.name: Arignar Anna Zoological Park
places.shortDescription: The Vandalur Zoo, a huge park on the south-western side of Chennai, 32 km from the city centre.
places.description: A large zoo with open moated enclosures, lions, safari rides and aviaries. It takes the better part of a day, and battery cars are available.

places.name: Guindy National Park
places.shortDescription: One of India's few national parks inside a city, at just 2.7 sq km, home to blackbuck and deer.
places.description: A small scrap of scrub forest inside the city, on the grounds of the Governor's residence, with a children's park and snake farm at the entrance.

places.name: Pancha Rathas
places.shortDescription: Five monolithic chariot temples at Mamallapuram, each carved from one rock in the Pallava era.
places.description: Five shrines, each in a different form, along with a stone lion, elephant and bull. They look built, but each was cut from a single rock.
places.history: Part of the UNESCO-listed group at Mahabalipuram, carved under the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I.

places.name: Arjuna's Penance
places.shortDescription: A huge rock relief at Mamallapuram, one of the largest open-air bas-reliefs in the world.
places.description: Over a hundred figures of gods, people and animals crowd a giant boulder face. A natural cleft down the middle represents the descent of the Ganges.
places.history: Measuring 96 by 43 feet, it was carved in the 7th century under the Pallavas.

places.name: Kailasanathar Temple
places.shortDescription: The oldest structural temple in Kanchipuram, a small Pallava masterpiece in sandstone.
places.description: A quiet sandstone temple with a row of small chapels around the courtyard. The faded murals and rearing lion pillars feel a long way from the busy temples of the town.
places.history: One of the oldest surviving monuments in Kanchipuram, built by the Pallavas.

places.name: Ekambareswarar Temple
places.shortDescription: A big Shiva temple in Kanchipuram with a tall gopuram and an old mango tree in the courtyard.
places.description: One of the five great Shiva temples representing the elements, this one being earth. It has a long thousand-pillared hall, and a sacred mango tree stands in its courtyard.

places.name: Kamakshi Amman Temple
places.shortDescription: One of the great goddess temples of south India, in the historic city of Kanchipuram.
places.description: A golden tower rises above the temple of Kamakshi, and it's closely linked to the Kanchi monastery. Kanchipuram's famous silk shops are only a short walk away.

places.name: Thanjavur Maratha Palace
places.shortDescription: The palace of the Bhonsle kings of Tanjore, with an art gallery and a historic library.
places.description: Rambling halls contain a superb collection of Chola bronzes, while the Saraswathi Mahal Library has palm-leaf manuscripts. Climb the bell tower for a view of the Big Temple.
places.history: The official residence of the Bhonsle family, who ruled Tanjore from 1674 to 1855.

places.name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram
places.shortDescription: The capital built by Rajendra I around 1025, with a UNESCO-listed temple that rivals Thanjavur's.
places.description: All that's left of a great royal city is its great temple and its huge Nandi. It's far quieter than Thanjavur and very beautiful, with curved tower lines.
places.history: Rajendra I founded it in about 1025 to mark his Chola army's march to the Ganges.

places.name: Airavatesvara Temple
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed Chola jewel at Darasuram, near Kumbakonam, with tiny, detailed carving.
places.description: Smaller than the other great Chola temples, it's covered in carving so tiny and fine you need to stand close. The front hall is shaped like a chariot.
places.history: Built by the Chola emperor Rajaraja II in the 12th century.

places.name: Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam
places.shortDescription: One of the largest working temple complexes in the world, on an island in the Kaveri.
places.description: Seven walled enclosures, with a whole town of shops and houses living inside the outer ones. The Rajagopuram is among the tallest temple towers in Asia.
places.history: One of the most important Vaishnava sites, developed over many centuries.

places.name: Jambukeswarar Temple
places.shortDescription: A Shiva temple at Thiruvanaikaval, one of five representing the elements, this one water.
places.description: Long, quiet corridors surround a low sanctum where a spring keeps the floor damp. It's just down the road from Srirangam, and much calmer.

places.name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal
places.shortDescription: The grand 1636 palace of Tirumala Nayaka in Madurai, 2 km from the Meenakshi Temple.
places.description: Giant white pillars ring a courtyard of huge proportions, in a blend of Dravidian and Islamic styles. What's left is a fraction of the original.
places.history: Built by Tirumala Nayaka, who ruled Madurai from 1623 to 1659.

places.name: Doddabetta
places.shortDescription: The highest peak in the Nilgiris at 2,637 m, 9 km from Ooty, with a telescope house on top.
places.description: A road reaches the summit, which has a telescope house and views out over the Nilgiris and on clear days down to the plains.

places.name: Ooty Lake
places.shortDescription: An artificial lake and boathouse in Ooty, built in the 19th century by John Sullivan.
places.description: A long, slender lake at the edge of town, with rowing boats and a small amusement area. It's touristy, but it is the classic Ooty outing.

places.name: Government Botanical Garden
places.shortDescription: Ooty's great terraced garden, laid out in 1848, with a fossil tree and a Toda hut.
places.description: Twenty-two hectares of lawns, lily ponds and old trees, climbing the slope of a hill. The flower show each May is the highlight of the Ooty summer season.
places.history: Laid out in 1848.

places.name: Mudumalai National Park
places.shortDescription: A tiger reserve in the Nilgiris with a famous elephant camp at Theppakadu.
places.description: Dry forest and river valleys shared with Bandipur and Wayanad. Elephants are easy to see, and the Theppakadu camp is the one in the Oscar-winning film The Elephant Whisperers.

places.name: Sim's Park
places.shortDescription: A 19th-century garden at Coonoor, with many rare trees from around the world.
places.description: A small hillside garden in the cooler, quieter hill town of Coonoor, full of old specimen trees. It's a stop on the Nilgiri Mountain Railway line.

places.name: Kodaikanal Lake
places.shortDescription: A star-shaped man-made lake at the centre of Kodaikanal, created in 1863.
places.description: A 5 km road and cycle path goes around the lake, with boathouses and horse rides. It's the town's centre and its most popular walk.
places.history: Sir Vere Henry Levinge, then the Collector of Madurai, was instrumental in creating the lake in 1863.

places.name: Dhandayuthapani Swamy Temple
places.shortDescription: The hilltop Murugan temple at Palani, one of the Six Abodes of Murugan.
places.description: A flight of 693 steps, a winch railway and a ropeway all reach this popular temple on a hill. Its idol is made of a sacred mixture of nine herbs, and pilgrims come bearing kavadi.

places.name: Yercaud
places.shortDescription: A quiet coffee hill station at 1,515 m in the Eastern Ghats, in Salem district.
places.description: Coffee and pepper estates around a small lake, with viewpoints across the plains. It's a cheaper, calmer alternative to Ooty and Kodaikanal.

places.name: Anamalai Tiger Reserve
places.shortDescription: A rich forest in the Anaimalai Hills, near Pollachi, home to lion-tailed macaques and elephants.
places.description: Tall forest and tea around Topslip and the Valparai plateau. It's one of the best places in India for wildlife that's rare elsewhere, like the lion-tailed macaque.

places.name: Hogenakkal Falls
places.shortDescription: A waterfall on the Kaveri, where you ride round coracle boats right up to the falling water.
places.description: The river falls over rock channels, and round wicker coracles take visitors around the pools. It's on the Tamil Nadu and Karnataka border, 46 km from Dharmapuri.

places.name: Courtallam
places.shortDescription: A town of waterfalls in the Tenkasi foothills, with bathing pools thought to have healing power.
places.description: Water falling through spice forest gives this place the name Spa of South India. Season peaks when the southwest monsoon arrives.

places.name: Arunachalesvara Temple
places.shortDescription: A vast Shiva temple at the foot of Arunachala hill, representing the element of fire.
places.description: A huge temple with four great gopurams and a nine-storey tower. Pilgrims walk the 14 km around Arunachala at the full moon, and it's also the place of Ramana Maharshi's ashram.

places.name: Gingee Fort
places.shortDescription: A fort spread over three hills, known as the Great Wall of South India.
places.description: Walls link three rocky hills in one of the best forts in Tamil Nadu. Climb Rajagiri for a hard scramble, and pass a tall Kalyana Mahal on the way.
places.history: It lies 160 km from Chennai, and the Marathas considered it an unbeatable fortress.

places.name: Nataraja Temple, Chidambaram
places.shortDescription: The great temple of Shiva as the lord of the dance, a key site in Tamil Hinduism.
places.description: A golden roof sits above the hall of the dancing Shiva. Reliefs of the 108 dance poses of Bharatanatyam are on the gates.
places.history: Chola kings made Nataraja their family deity and gave the temple its golden roof.

places.name: Pichavaram Mangrove
places.shortDescription: One of the world's largest mangrove forests, explored by rowing boat through narrow channels.
places.description: A maze of green channels near Chidambaram, between the Vellar and Coleroon estuaries, reached by rowing boat. It's quiet and full of birds in winter.

places.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health
places.shortDescription: The Velankanni shrine, one of India's biggest Christian pilgrimage sites, on the Bay of Bengal.
places.description: A white Gothic basilica by the sea, visited by pilgrims of all faiths. The nine-day festival around 8 September draws huge crowds.
highlights: Annual festival in late August and September

sources.title: Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health, Velankanni – Wikipedia

images.alt: Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health, Nagapattinam

places.name: Point Calimere Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A coastal reserve at Point Calimere, known for its blackbuck and huge flocks of flamingos.
places.description: Coastal forest and salt marsh at the southeastern tip of Nagapattinam district. Flamingos and other waders arrive in large numbers each winter.

sources.title: Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary – Wikipedia

places.name: Vellore Fort
places.shortDescription: A 16th-century moated stone fort at the heart of Vellore, built under the Vijayanagara empire.
places.description: Huge granite walls and a wide moat enclose a temple, a mosque and a church, a good example of its history. The Vellore Mutiny of 1806 began here.
places.history: Built by the Nayakas Chinna Bommi Reddy and Timma Reddy, under the Vijayanagara empire.

places.name: Sri Lakshmi Narayani Golden Temple
places.shortDescription: A modern temple at Sripuram, Vellore, coated in gold and set in a star-shaped path.
places.description: A shining golden shrine at the end of a star-shaped walkway, which is impressive when lit up at night. Wear modest clothes, and leave your phone at the entrance.

sources.title: Sri Lakshmi Narayani Golden Temple – Wikipedia

images.alt: Sri Lakshmi Narayani Golden Temple, Vellore

places.name: Dhanushkodi
places.shortDescription: An abandoned town at the tip of Pamban Island, about 24 km from Sri Lanka across the sea.
places.description: A strip of sand running out to sea, with the ruins of a church and a railway station. The 1964 cyclone wiped the town out, and it was never rebuilt.
places.history: Destroyed in the Rameswaram cyclone of 1964.

places.name: Pamban Bridge
places.shortDescription: India's first sea bridge, from 1914, linking Rameswaram to the mainland across the Palk Strait.
places.description: The old cantilever railway bridge runs alongside the new one over turquoise water. You can see them both from the road bridge, a popular place to stop for a photo.
places.history: Opened on 24 February 1914, it stayed India's longest sea bridge for decades.

places.name: Thiruvalluvar Statue
places.shortDescription: A 40.6 m tall stone statue of the Tamil poet, on a small rock island off Kanyakumari.
places.description: A ferry takes visitors to this huge statue next to the Vivekananda Rock Memorial, where three seas meet.
places.history: The poet wrote the Thirukkural, a classic Tamil work on ethics. The statue was unveiled in 2000.

places.name: Padmanabhapuram Palace
places.shortDescription: A vast wooden palace from the Travancore era, the finest example of Kerala's traditional architecture.
places.description: Rosewood ceilings, carved beds and a large hall of black-polished floors. It lies in Tamil Nadu, but it's run by the government of Kerala.
places.history: Also known as Kalkulam Palace. It was the Travancore kingdom's old seat before the capital moved to Thiruvananthapuram.
